speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned weakness and decreased sensation in your right arm; can you tell me if these symptoms started suddenly or developed gradually?

speaker: Patient
text: 55-year-old male bodybuilder. The patient has been experiencing weakness in his right arm for a few weeks, which has progressively worsened to the point of dropping objects. He also reports a recent unexplained weight loss of 17 pounds and has a history of diabetes. The patient admits to chronic alcohol use, heavy smoking, and anabolic steroid use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pancoast tumor (superior sulcus tumor) causing right arm weakness and decreased sensation, likely due to Pancoast syndrome involving T1/T2 nerve root or brachial plexus compression.

REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray and MRI_Chest_Axial
